title: Does a Hybrid Space-Aware Randomized Defense Improve Empirical and Certified Adversarial Robustness?
claim: A hybrid block injects randomness in both weight space and feature space, built from a stochastic perturbed-weight convolution module.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; block overview plus zoomed internal diagram, legend box
description: Panel (a) shows the HySCAN block as a left-to-right flow. A panda input image from ImageNet passes through two RWAN modules, each labeled 'Implicit Stochasticity' and followed by a noisy feature-map thumbnail. A residual skip arrow loops beneath and rejoins at an element-wise addition node. A SANI module labeled 'Explicit Stochasticity' follows, then a final feature map. A gray legend box lists element-wise operators and arrow colors for BN+ReLU (pink) and Mean (blue). Panel (b), separated by a dashed line, expands RWAN. SANI produces a mean gate that is max-normalized, and Gaussian noise is added. A softplus-transformed trainable scalar and the deterministic convolution weight combine into a robust stochastic perturbed weight. The result is convolved with the input to give the RWAN output. Pastel colored boxes and math notation are used throughout.
caption: (a) Overview of the proposed HySCAN block, which replaces a standard convolutional block (e.g., the residual block in ResNet
abstract: We introduce Hybrid Space-aware Stochastic Convolution Attention Noise (HySCAN), a hybrid randomized defense that helps close the long-standing gap between provable robustness under ℓ2 certificates and empirical robustness against strong ℓ∞ attacks, while maintaining strong generalization across diverse imaging benchmarks. HySCAN jointly explores complementary sources of stochasticity at both training and inference: (i) implicit weight-space randomness via stochastic-aware Random Weights, and (ii) explicit feature-space randomness via Stochastic Attention Noise Injection modules. By incorporating randomness at both the parameter and representation levels, HySCAN enables meaningful certified guarantees while improving empirical robustness in practice. Comprehensive experiments on diverse imaging datasets, e.g., CelebA, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, HAM10000, and NIH Chest X-ray, demonstrate that HySCAN outperforms existing certified and empirical defenses, improving certified robustness by up to ≈ 9.6% and empirical robustness by up to ≈ 5% without reducing clean accuracy.
